questions.prompt: You wrote a release workflow skill for yourself and left it in ~/.claude/skills/. A teammate says they don't have it and asks you to send it over. What is actually wrong?
options: Personal skills are machine-local by definition — a teammate will never see them, and the fix is project scope, committed to the repo
The install failed silently; re-copy the folder to ~/.claude/skills/ on their machine
They need to run claude plugin validate before personal skills appear
The skill's name is refused because it isn't lowercase
questions.explanation: Scope is the whole mechanism here: personal skills load on this user, this machine, and nowhere else — so a teammate not having one is correct behaviour, not a failed install. The fix is to move it to .claude/skills/ and commit it. Option B asks a teammate to copy a file into a machine-local location that will diverge immediately. Option C is unrelated — validate checks frontmatter parsing on a skills directory, not who can see it. Option D invents a naming rule; names are rejected for specific characters, not case.

questions.prompt: A skill you installed runs fine as /my-skill but never fires on a natural request. The description looks correct. What is the diagnostic order?
options: Re-read the description out loud and rewrite it more emphatically
Check /skills first to confirm discovery, then claude plugin validate the directory for unparseable frontmatter
Check ~/.claude/skills/.trash/ in case a sweep moved it
questions.explanation: The symptom has two causes that look identical from outside — a description that doesn't match human phrasing, and frontmatter that fails to parse so the body loads with empty metadata — and only a parse check separates them. /skills first establishes that discovery is even the problem; validate then names the file. Option A tests a hypothesis you said you'd already ruled out. Option C destroys the evidence that would have told you which cause it was. Option D is a real failure mode but it removes the skill from the menu entirely, which is not the symptom described.

questions.prompt: A colleague's eleven personal skills vanished between sessions with no error, and their folders are gone from ~/.claude/skills/. Where do they actually go?
options: They are deleted permanently the moment they stop loading
They are moved into a timestamped folder under ~/.claude/skills/.trash/, recoverable until the retention sweep — historically triggered by a stray manifest.json in the skills directory
They moved into ~/.claude/skills/synced/, which is where downloaded skills live
They were overridden by a plugin with the same names
questions.explanation: This is a reported failure shape, not a hypothetical: a file named manifest.json in the skills directory used to make Claude Code sweep the listed skill folders into ~/.claude/skills/.trash/ under a timestamped subfolder, and those skills stopped loading — with a 30-day retention sweep afterwards. So recovery is a move, and it is time-limited. Option A is the panic response and it's wrong. Option C confuses two different things — synced skills are downloaded, not swept. Option D would change what commands exist, not remove files.
